cards.title: Unlocking history
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: It addresses the intersection of cultural heritage, economic policy, and international relations within the context of regional organizations like the SCO and ECO.
cards.summary: Lahore has been named the ECO Tourism Capital for 2027, following its selection as the SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27. This recognition offers a significant opportunity to boost Pakistan's heritage economy and improve international standing. However, the government must prioritize professional conservation, better infrastructure, and enhanced security over mere cultural events to ensure long-term tourism success.
key_facts: Lahore was selected as the SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026 to 2027.
Lahore has been designated as the ECO Tourism Capital for 2027.
Sustainable heritage tourism requires specialised training, improved clean air, and infrastructure investment.

vocab.meaning: A feeling of uncritical satisfaction with one's achievements.

text: LAHORE, a living archive of history, is having a moment in the sun. After the city’s selection as the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026 to 2027 by the SCO, it now assumes the title of the ECO Tourism Capital for 2027. Not only does this put Pakistan’s cultural and historical wealth on the world stage, it also showcases the country’s syncretic values. Undoubtedly, this is a tremendous chance to expand our heritage economy with regional support. While the Punjab government has made positive interventions to preserve many iconic remnants that dot Lahore, consequential inputs from historians and conservation experts are missing in the country. International recognition brings great responsibility. Economic salvation for Lahore’s inheritance requires investment in specialised training, clean air, security, and conservation efforts guided by international techniques so that the character of antiquity is not lost.

Cultural activities alone are never enough. Tourism will thrive once proper infrastructure is in place, and the tendency to treat preservation as an added expense for a fragile economy is abandoned. The large-scale project entails lenient visa policies and heightened security, an easy transport network, tour guides, site-related literature, small hotels and rest houses, amplified through local and international publicity. Meanwhile, seasonal festivals and traditions planned around heritage sites highlight Pakistan’s inclusivity for all visitors. Importantly, civilisational heirlooms extend beyond Punjab and so should such infrastructure. Every province promises a tourism boom, which is both a shot in the arm for the economy, and a driver of robust bonds with other countries. In short, there is little time for complacency. Every citizen has the right to benefit from national treasures, which comprise cuisine, languages, communities, and customs. Historical places in most parts are on the verge of caving in due to neglect. To rewrite the unflattering narratives about Pakistan it is crucial that life return to our priceless sites.

cards.title: Wage enforcement
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: It highlights core governance failures regarding labour rights and wage law enforcement, relevant to Pakistan Affairs and Governance papers.
cards.summary: The finance ministry has finally ordered public departments to comply with minimum wage regulations after failing to implement new rates for four months. The editorial criticizes government bodies for prioritizing senior executive benefits while neglecting the legal rights of low-paid employees. It calls for stricter labour inspections and better enforcement mechanisms for both public and private sector employers.
key_facts: Government organisations failed to increase worker wages four months after the official announcement of new rates.
Parliamentary committees had to intervene to force compliance with legal minimum wage requirements.
Labour inspectors are needed to verify actual payments to workers, especially those on temporary contracts.

vocab.meaning: The action of following a rule or order.

text: THE finance ministry’s order asking ministries, departments and public bodies to confirm that they pay workers the minimum wage is welcome, though long overdue. It is troubling that a parliamentary committee had to step in because government organisations had failed to increase workers’ wages four months after the new rates were announced. The committee rightly questioned why senior officials are quick to raise their own salaries and benefits but slow to do the same for low-paid workers. Paying salaries through banks and requiring departments to report whether they follow the rules should make it easier to identify violations. But reports alone are not enough. The government must check salary records, ensure that workers receive any unpaid wages and punish departments that break the rules. Workers should not have to rely on parliament to secure wages they are already entitled to under the law. The government cannot expect private businesses to follow minimum wage laws when its own departments fail to do so. Such failures only encourage private employers to ignore the law.

Yet violations are hardly confined to government offices. Many private employers pay workers less than the legal minimum, particularly those hired on temporary contracts or through contractors. Such arrangements must not become an excuse to deny workers their rightful wages or allow employers to escape responsibility. Labour inspectors must check what workers are actually paid. The provinces, which have different minimum wage rates, must also ensure that employers follow the law. This requires regular inspections, a simple way for workers to report violations, and penalties for employers who refuse to comply. Workers who report underpayment must also be protected from losing their jobs or facing punishment. Without such protection, many will stay silent rather than risk their livelihoods. The law must also protect domestic workers. In affluent households, domestic workers often labour long hours for a pittance, with little power to demand better pay or treatment. Their work takes place behind closed doors, making abuses harder to detect and leaving them with few ways to complain. A minimum wage is meaningful only when even the least visible worker can rely on it.

cards.title: Fresh elections?
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: It outlines the current political instability and the friction between coalition partners, which is essential for understanding contemporary democratic processes in Pakistan.
cards.summary: The political landscape is shifting as the PPP and PML-N differ over the proposal to create new provinces. While some government leaders support a referendum on the matter, others suggest the current focus should remain on electoral reforms. The situation remains fluid with no clear consensus on whether to prioritize early elections or provincial restructuring.
key_facts: PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari expressed opposition to the division of provinces.
PML-N ministers have expressed support for the idea of holding a referendum on new provinces.
The PPP leadership has acknowledged that neither a referendum nor fresh elections can occur before the completion of electoral reforms.
